question: What is the meaning of weight in relation to physical properties?
description: Weight is a physical property that refers to the force exerted on an object due to gravity. It is an important aspect of materials and products, especially for structural elements like steel beams. However, its relevance may vary depending on the type of material or product, such as flooring or doors. In the context of sustainable construction, understanding the weight of materials can help in optimizing their use, reducing transportation costs, and promoting circular economy practices. For instance, lighter materials can be more energy-efficient and easier to recycle.

3.1.3
Composition properties
Figure 5 shows the composition property facet. This block of ontology helps to optimise
the selection, processing, and assembly of the constituent parts and materials of a product
and facilitates their separation, dismantling, and recycling at the end of life of a product
to maximise the circularity.
Figure 5: Composition property facet of the MPO.
CompositionProperty has two subclasses, ConstituentPart and ConstituentMaterial. For
example, crossbeam has constituent materials carbon fibre, glass fibre, epoxy resin, alu-
minium, foam, and film adhesive that have mass, and a source and destination in a circular
economy.
